title: Machine-learning metabolomics prioritizes succinate in sepsis-associated encephalopathy
summary: In plasma samples from 29 controls, 32 sepsis patients and 27 patients with sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE), LC–MS/MS plus machine-learning feature selection identified a 12-metabolite profile. Succinate rose stepwise from controls to sepsis to SAE, ranked among the five leading XGBoost features, and correlated with APACHE II, SOFA and lactate. In a cecal-ligation-and-puncture mouse model, dietary succinate supplementation before sepsis worsened cognitive-test performance, neuronal injury and microglial activation; succinate also increased inflammatory gene expression in cultured microglia.
ai_technology: Random forest and support-vector-machine feature ranking with XGBoost classification
organization: Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology

evidence.tested: In a cecal-ligation-and-puncture mouse model, dietary succinate supplementation before sepsis worsened cognitive-test performance, neuronal injury and microglial activation; succinate also increased inflammatory gene expression in cultured microglia.
evidence.unknown: The human discovery cohort comprised 88 participants and the held-out model test set had 18 participants, so diagnostic performance and metabolite ranking need larger external cohorts. Succinate supplementation was given before CLP in mice, and cell experiments used a microglial cell line; these are preclinical perturbations and do not prove that succinate causes human SAE or that targeting it improves patient outcomes. Associations with severity scores are observational.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning feature selection and classifier comparison were applied to the measured plasma metabolomics to identify discriminatory features; succinate ranked among the top five XGBoost features. Researchers then tested its functional relevance through supplementation in a mouse sepsis model and in cultured microglia. The animal/cell experiments were human-directed follow-up, not model-generated predictions.
